title: Sounds and Spelling
audience: True beginner. Assume nothing: not what an accent mark is, not why letters go silent.
model_voice: Marie (clear standard French) for explanations and drills. Camille and Mathieu (Québec) for the Hear it in Canada clip in each lesson.

lessons.title: How French works
lessons.goal: Know that French spelling is not read like English, that most final letters are silent, and that French has even rhythm with no stressed syllables.
lessons.canada_note: Words you already know from Canadian signs (sortie, arrêt, ouvert, fermé) read aloud.

lessons.title: The alphabet and spelling your name
lessons.goal: Say all 26 letter names and spell your own name and email aloud.
lessons.canada_note: Spelling out a name on the phone with Service Canada, a clinic or a landlord.

lessons.title: Accent marks
lessons.goal: Tell é, è, ê, ë, à, â, ù, û, ô, î, ï, ç and œ apart. Know which change the sound (é vs è) and which only change spelling.
lessons.canada_note: Reading names and street names with accents (Montréal, Québec, Rue Saint-Jacques).

lessons.title: Core vowels
lessons.goal: Say a, e (three different e sounds), i, o, u and the pairs ai/ei, au/eau, oi, eu.
lessons.canada_note: Hear how long vowels become diphthongs in Québec (fête, pâte).

lessons.title: u vs ou and the rounded vowels
lessons.goal: Tell u from ou, eu from ou, and say them. Minimal pairs: dessus/dessous, tu/tout, rue/roue.
lessons.canada_note: Hear short u/i/ou become relaxed in Québec (petite, lune).

lessons.title: Nasal vowels
lessons.goal: Recognise and say an/en, on, in/ain/ein, un. Minimal pairs: banc/bon/bain, vent/vont/vin.

lessons.title: Consonants and silent letters
lessons.goal: Know which final consonants are silent and the CaReFuL exceptions (c, r, f, l). Say c/ç, g/gu, qu, ch, gn, j, s between vowels, h (silent). Know th and ph.
lessons.canada_note: Affrication: t and d before i/u sound like ts/dz in Québec (tu, dire).

lessons.title: The French r
lessons.goal: Produce a usable French r in the throat, in initial, medial and final position.
lessons.canada_note: Québec r variants. A clear standard r is enough for the exam.

lessons.title: Liaison, enchaînement and élision
lessons.goal: Explain and apply: les amis (lez-amis), un ami, il est ici. Forbidden after et. Elision: le+ami = l'ami, je+ai = j'ai, ce+est = c'est.
lessons.canada_note: Fast Canadian speech: je suis becomes chu, tu es becomes t'es.

lessons.title: Numbers 0 to 20
lessons.goal: Hear and say 0 to 20 and read them in a phone number, a time and a price.
lessons.canada_note: Postal codes, 911, phone numbers, bus numbers.

lessons.title: Numbers 20 to 1000 and beyond
lessons.goal: Hear and say 20 to 100 (soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix), hundreds, thousands. Note that Québec and France both use soixante-dix and quatre-vingt-dix.
lessons.canada_note: Prices in dollars and cents, rent, salaries, years and dates.

lessons.title: Rhythm, intonation and questions
lessons.goal: Say short sentences with even rhythm, rising intonation for yes/no questions, falling for statements.
lessons.canada_note: Canadian intonation patterns in everyday questions.

lessons.title: Hear it in Canada: a first listening
lessons.goal: Understand a short clear Canadian French message and a short France French message, and notice what differs.
lessons.canada_note: Introduces the accent variety the exam can contain.
